q: A mutation is a change in a gene or a chromosome that may cause a change in a ____ characteristic.
e: A mutation is a change in a gene or a chromosome that may cause a change in a phenotypic characteristic. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: Mutations that occur in body cells will only affect the particular cell in which they ____.
e: Mutations that occur in body cells will only affect the particular cell in which they occur. Occur is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Only mutation in sex cells (gametes), or in the cell that divide to form gametes, can be passed on to the next generation and genetic diseases can be ____.
e: Only mutation in sex cells (gametes), or in the cell that divide to form gametes, can be passed on to the next generation and genetic diseases can be formed. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait. Gametes are sex cells: sperm and eggs, produced by meiosis.

q: Bits of chromosomes can sometimes break off from one chromosome and become attached to another. These 'mistakes' are called ____.
e: Bits of chromosomes can sometimes break off from one chromosome and become attached to another. These 'mistakes' are called chromosome mutations. Chromosome mutations change structure or number of whole chromosomes. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: One relatively common chromosome mutation results in ova containing two copies of chromosome ____.
e: One relatively common chromosome mutation results in ova containing two copies of chromosome 21. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: The zygote will have three copies of chromosome 21. This is called trisomy of chromosome ____.
e: The zygote will have three copies of chromosome 21. This is called trisomy of chromosome 21. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. Dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts.

q: The condition that results is Down's ____.
e: The condition that results is Down's syndrome. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome.

q: Down's syndrome is more common in babies born by women over ____ years of age than by younger women.
e: Down's syndrome is more common in babies born by women over 40 years of age than by younger women. Down's syndrome comes from an extra chromosome 21. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome.

q: A change in the nucleotide sequences of a DNA molecule is termed as ____.
e: A change in the nucleotide sequences of a DNA molecule is termed as gene mutation. A gene mutation changes the base sequence of one gene. A nucleotide is a sugar, a phosphate, and a nitrogen base.

q: The order of DNA bases in a gene determines the order of amino acids in a particular ____.
e: The order of DNA bases in a gene determines the order of amino acids in a particular protein. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Amino acids have an amine group and a carboxyl group around a central carbon.

q: If a mutation occurs in a gene, the primary structure of the protein it codes for could be ____.
e: If a mutation occurs in a gene, the primary structure of the protein it codes for could be altered. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: Albinism is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for the enzyme that produce ____.
e: Albinism is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for the enzyme that produce melanin. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up.

q: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for CFTR protein that transport ____ ions.
e: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for CFTR protein that transport chloride ions. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: Sickle-cell anemia is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for the B-chain of ____.
e: Sickle-cell anemia is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for the B-chain of haemoglobin. Haemoglobin in red blood cells binds oxygen for transport. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: Huntington's disease is caused by a mutation in HD gene located on chromosome ____.
e: Huntington's disease is caused by a mutation in HD gene located on chromosome 4. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: Mutations are caused by damage to DNA or by a failure in the DNA copying process that occurs before nuclear division in ____.
e: Mutations are caused by damage to DNA or by a failure in the DNA copying process that occurs before nuclear division in cells. The cell is the basic living unit; tissues are groups of similar cells. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides.

q: Ultra-violet radiation, X-rays and gamma rays are the most damaging ____.
e: Ultra-violet radiation, X-rays and gamma rays are the most damaging radiation. Radiation is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Benzpyrene in cigarette smoke causes ____.
e: Benzpyrene in cigarette smoke causes mutation. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: The agents that cause mutation are called ____.
e: The agents that cause mutation are called mutagens. Physical mutagens include radiation; chemical mutagens include some drugs and pollutants. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: Variation is the differences that exist within a ____.
e: Variation is the differences that exist within a species. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring.

q: Gene mutation is the only way in which completely new genetic material is ____.
e: Gene mutation is the only way in which completely new genetic material is produced. A gene mutation changes the base sequence of one gene. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: During meiosis, the alleles of different genes are 'shuffled' to give new combinations in the ____.
e: During meiosis, the alleles of different genes are 'shuffled' to give new combinations in the gametes. Gametes are sex cells: sperm and eggs, produced by meiosis. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles.

q: Gene mutation, meiosis and fertilization give rise to variation between individuals in every ____.
e: Gene mutation, meiosis and fertilization give rise to variation between individuals in every generation. A gene mutation changes the base sequence of one gene. A mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: Continuous variation shows no clear cut distinction between the different traits of a characteristic, e.g. height, weight, intelligence, skin colour, number of seeds in a ____.
e: Continuous variation shows no clear cut distinction between the different traits of a characteristic, e.g. Height, weight, intelligence, skin colour, number of seeds in a pod. Continuous culture keeps adding nutrients and taking product for a long run. Skin is a surface for some heat exchange and a barrier, but most large animals also need lungs or gills.

q: Discontinuous variation shows a clear cut distinction between two traits, e.g. eye and skin colour (pigmented or non-pigmented), left-handed/right-handed, ability/inability to roll the ____.
e: Discontinuous variation shows a clear cut distinction between two traits, e.g. Eye and skin colour (pigmented or non-pigmented), left-handed/right-handed, ability/inability to roll the tongue. Skin is a surface for some heat exchange and a barrier, but most large animals also need lungs or gills. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.
